record.paper_title: Open problems on compact constant mean curvature surfaces with boundary
record.context_brief: closed cmc surfaces in a critical-width slab
record.original_question: Is the round sphere of radius 1/H the only closed H-surface contained in the closure of a slab of width 2/|H|?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.5. Is the sphere of radius 1/H the only closed H-surface included in the closure of a slab of width 2/|H|?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $H>0$. A closed (compact, without boundary) smooth orientable immersed surface $\Sigma \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ is called an $H$-surface if its mean curvature is constant and equal to $H$ everywhere. A slab of width $w>0$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is a closed region bounded by two parallel planes at distance $w$ apart. The round sphere of radius $1/H$ is an $H$-surface, and it fits inside the closure of a slab of width $2/H$.

Question: Is the round sphere of radius $1/H$ the only closed $H$-surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ that is contained in the closure of some slab of width $2/H$?
